_readme: Golden vectors for the 8-byte envelope header defined in docs/PROTOCOL.md §3
(HLD §5 asks for these explicitly: 'goldens tested in CI'). Every byte in
'header_hex' and 'full_hex' below was derived by hand from §3's field layout
and §0's 'all integers are little-endian' rule -- NOT by running
EncodeEnvelope and recording its output. A vector produced that way can
never fail and defeats the purpose of this test (track X4).
Header layout (§3): byte 0 = ver (u8), byte 1 = capID (u8), bytes 2-3 =
msgType (u16 LE), bytes 4-7 = length (u32 LE), followed by `length` bytes
of payload.
D-34 offset rule, as actually applied (confirmed against
internal/session/convert.go and internal/wire/openair/v1/*.pb.go, which
landed concurrently with this track):
- capID IS offset by one from the generated CapabilityId enum (wire 0 =
control = enum 1; wire 1 = files = enum CAPABILITY_ID_FILES = 2; wire 2
= clipboard = enum 3). PROTOCOL.md §3 states this explicitly for capID.
- Per-capability msgType enums (ControlMessageType, FilesMessageType,
ClipboardMessageType, ...) are NOT offset. The wire msgType equals the
generated enum's raw int32 value directly. See the 'ambiguity' note
below -- this is not actually stated anywhere in §3 itself, and had to
be confirmed by reading the generated code.
Ambiguity/defect notes found while deriving these vectors (worker report,
track X4, has the full writeup):
1. §3's general sentence ('every enum in the schemas is offset by one')
reads as if it covers msgType too, but the sentence that follows only
lists capID, TrustLevel, ProtectionTier, ConsentScope and PathClass as
offset fields -- msgType enums are conspicuously absent from that
list. The generated code confirms the omission is deliberate:
CapabilityId values carry a '// wire N' comment in common.pb.go;
ControlMessageType/FilesMessageType/etc. carry no such comment, and
internal/session/convert.go (M1a) states outright that msgType is 'NOT
offset either' and that PROTOCOL.md 'never enumerated msgType at all'.
§3 should say so explicitly instead of leaving it to be inferred from
an absence in a list.
2. §3 says an unknown `ver` closes the connection with
`PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`. §10's error code table defines a separate,
more specific code for exactly this condition: 0x02 UNKNOWN_VERSION,
'Unsupported envelope version'. §3's prose and §10's table disagree
about which code an unknown version maps to. internal/session/envelope.go
(M1a) hit this independently and chose to follow §3's literal text
(CodeProtocolViolation) with a comment flagging the inconsistency --
this vector file follows the shipped implementation for that same
reason (§3 is the more specific normative statement about this exact
byte), but the inconsistency itself belongs in docs/decision-tree.md.
File format: JSON manifest + hex-encoded byte strings, chosen so a human
can check 'header_hex' against the §3 diagram by hand without tooling.
The two 16-MiB-adjacent cases store a payload *pattern* description
instead of literal payload bytes (33MB of hex would make this file useless
to review); only the 8-byte header -- the part actually derived from the
spec -- is stored as a literal golden value for those cases.

cases.name: control_hello
cases.protocol_clause: PROTOCOL.md §3 header diagram; Appendix B capID 0 = control ('0 is the session layer itself')
cases.description: A plain session-layer (control) message with a small nonempty payload. Baseline case: pins the general 8-byte header layout and field order (ver, capID, msgType LE, length LE) with no boundary conditions in play.

fields.cap_id_note: control capability, Appendix B wire value 0. Generated enum CapabilityId_CAPABILITY_ID_CONTROL = 1 (D-34: capID wire = enum - 1).
fields.msg_type_note: ControlMessageType_CONTROL_MESSAGE_TYPE_HELLO = 1 in internal/wire/openair/v1/session.pb.go. msgType wire value equals the raw generated enum int directly -- see ambiguity note 1 in _readme.

cases.name: files_capability_wire_offset
cases.protocol_clause: PROTOCOL.md §3: 'Wire values are not enum values... The capID byte for files is 0x01; CAPABILITY_ID_FILES is 2' (D-34)
cases.description: The D-34 pin: capID on the wire is 1 for files while the generated enum CAPABILITY_ID_FILES is 2. This is exactly the kind of regression this track exists to catch -- an encoder that casts the enum instead of converting it would write 0x02 here instead of 0x01.

fields.cap_id_note: files capability, Appendix B wire value 1. Confirmed against internal/wire/openair/v1/common.pb.go: CapabilityId_CAPABILITY_ID_FILES = 2 // wire 1.

cases.name: empty_payload
cases.description: Zero-length payload. Pins that length=0 is a valid, non-error encoding -- the header is complete on its own and no payload bytes follow.

cases.name: one_byte_payload
cases.description: Smallest nonzero payload (1 byte). Also exercises a second capID off-by-one instance (clipboard) alongside the files case.

fields.cap_id_note: clipboard capability, Appendix B wire value 2. Generated enum CapabilityId_CAPABILITY_ID_CLIPBOARD = 3 (D-34, second instance of the offset).

cases.name: multibyte_msgtype_endianness
cases.description: msgType = 0x1234, a value with distinct high and low bytes so the header unambiguously shows byte order: little-endian serializes it as 34 12, not 12 34. This value is a synthetic probe, not a real generated enum -- every real per-capability msgType enum observed in internal/wire/openair/v1/*.pb.go is small (well under 256) and would not exercise the high byte on its own.

fields.msg_type_note: 0x1234 = 4660 decimal. Synthetic value chosen only to pin byte order, not tied to any real ControlMessageType.

cases.name: boundary_max_message_size_exact
cases.protocol_clause: PROTOCOL.md §3: 'Receivers MUST reject length greater than 16 MiB'
cases.description: length is exactly MaxMessageSize (16777216 = 16 MiB). Read literally, §3 rejects lengths *greater than* the cap, so exactly-at-cap MUST be accepted, not rejected. Payload content itself pins nothing in §3 beyond 'payload is length bytes'; it is a repeating byte(i%256) pattern generated by the test rather than stored literally here, because 16 MiB of hex would make this file unreviewable by a human. The header_hex below -- the actual golden value, hand-derived from the u32 LE encoding of 16777216 -- is what this case exists to pin.

cases.name: error_length_exceeds_max
cases.protocol_clause: PROTOCOL.md §3: 'Receivers MUST reject length greater than 16 MiB with MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE'
cases.description: length = MaxMessageSize + 1 (16777217), one past the cap. Decode input is the 8-byte header only, with no payload bytes following it -- a correct decoder must reject based on the length field alone, before attempting to read a body that large (also guards against a hostile peer using an oversized length to force a huge allocation/read).

expect.error_reason: §3: 'Receivers MUST reject length greater than 16 MiB with MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE'; §10 code 0x03.

cases.name: error_unknown_version
cases.protocol_clause: PROTOCOL.md §3: 'A receiver seeing an unknown ver MUST close the connection with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION'
cases.description: ver = 2 (PROTOCOL.md defines only version 1; 2 chosen arbitrarily to mean 'anything unknown'). Must be rejected regardless of the rest of the frame being otherwise well-formed.

expect.error_reason: §3's prose names PROTOCOL_VIOLATION for this condition, but §10's error code table defines a separate, more specific 0x02 UNKNOWN_VERSION ('Unsupported envelope version') that reads like it exists for exactly this case. §3 and §10 disagree about which code an unknown version maps to -- see ambiguity note 2 in _readme. This vector follows the shipped implementation (internal/session/envelope.go), which follows §3's literal text and flags the same inconsistency in a comment.
